title: Handling and carrying guns at the ground
summary: An open gun, the gun rack, the gun slip and “ask before you touch”: how to handle a gun between stands.

body.html: This lesson adds the practical details to The core safety rules. Any gun, even an empty one, is handled with great care. Between stands you carry it open: an over-and-under broken (opened at the hinge), a semi-automatic with the action (the moving part that loads the cartridge) open. The muzzle points straight up or straight down.
Many shooters carry an open over-and-under over the forearm, with the barrels towards the ground. Slings and straps are not allowed on guns in either discipline.

When you are not using the gun, stand it upright in a gun rack or in another place the shooting ground provides. A semi-automatic stands there with its action open. Do not lean a gun against a car, a tree or a table: it can slip and fall.
Between the car and the shooting area, the gun travels in a gun slip or a hard case. Take it out only where the ground allows it, which is often not the car park.

Do not touch another person’s gun without the owner’s permission. If you would like to look at it, ask: the owner will open it and hand it to you. If someone asks to see that your gun is empty, open it and show the chambers. Coaches call this “show clear”.

Do not mount the gun (bring it up to your shoulder and cheek) and swing it as if you were following a target. This is called mock shooting. Both rulebooks forbid it, but they draw the line in different places.

html.sporting: Anywhere at the shooting ground: off the stand, on the stand before you call for a target, and while the targets are being shown.
html.compak: Outside the shooting positions, and while another squad member is shooting.

body.html: In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™, mock shooting or an accidental shot brings a warning the first time. If it happens again, the next target you hit is written down as a miss (zero).
To check that a gun works, use the test stand if the ground has one, usually near the clubhouse. Test shots on a competition stand are not allowed.

key_points.html: Carry the gun open, muzzle straight up or down; no slings
Not in use: upright in a gun rack, not leaning against things
A gun slip or case between the car and the shooting area
Ask before you touch another person’s gun; no mock shooting

did_you_know.html: An open gun is also a courtesy: it shows the people around you that they have nothing to worry about.

quiz.q: How do you carry a gun between stands?

options.text: Closed, on the shoulder, with the safety catch on
On a sling across the back, unloaded
Open, with the muzzle straight up or down

quiz.explain: The gun is carried open, muzzle up or down; slings are not allowed in either discipline.

quiz.q: Where does a gun go when you are not using it?

options.text: Upright in a gun rack or another place provided
Leaning against the car, closed and unloaded
Lying flat on the ground next to the stand

quiz.explain: Guns stand upright in a gun rack or another place the ground provides, so they cannot fall; a semi-automatic stands with its action open.

quiz.q: Where may you test-fire a gun?

options.text: On the first competition stand, before the round
On the test stand, if the ground has one
In a quiet corner of the car park

quiz.explain: Test shots belong on the test stand; firing them on a competition stand is forbidden.
